notes: TBox rule edit: every main-sequence star fuses helium into carbon in its core. Derivability very_unlikely: core hydrogen burning is what defines the main sequence (Wikipedia) and the rule is stated in general form ("fuse hydrogen into helium" 1,619 in Dolma). No exceptions: a star that no longer fuses hydrogen in its core has left the main sequence. Counterfactual: helium into carbon is what red giants do. The three derived queries name new stars (Kestrel-7, Orrin's Star, Tavrin-3) whose only route to an answer is the class rule plus the membership the prompt states (inheritance, 2 hops); they ask the pair, the fuel used up (an application) and the product, so the three answers differ. The direct question asks "and into what?", since a bare "hydrogen" was judged unclear against "hydrogen into helium". The conjunction puts its side fact first (two models answered "yes" to the earlier wording). The negation is worded "some main-sequence star does not ...", the logical negation of the universal. The near query asks what holds a main-sequence star together (gravity): same class, not about its fusion, and different from the new answer. Every bridge is stated in its prompt, so only the propositional side facts need checks.
